from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from storyboard and outline
        title_text = "Mapping Geometry to the Formula"
        lecture_lines = [
            "- Now let's map these shapes to the standard formula.",
            "- The numerator is the area of our target rectangle.",
            "- The denominator is the sum of all shaded areas.",
            "- Color-coded labels link the formula to the square's geometry.",
            "- Bayes' Theorem turns visual proportions into precise mathematical values."
        ]
        
        # Setup the scene layout
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        BLUE_COLOR = "#58C4DD"
        RED_COLOR = "#F44336"
        FORMULA_WHITE = "#FFFFFF"
        HIGHLIGHT_COLOR = "#FFFF00"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # L1: "Now let's map these shapes to the standard formula."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Create formula with subparts for highlighting
        # Indices: 0:P(H|E), 1:=, 2:\frac{, 3:P(H).P(E|H), 4:}{, 5:P(E), 6:}
        formula = MathTex(
            r"P(H|E)", "=", r"\frac{", r"P(H) \cdot P(E|H)", r"}{", r"P(E)", r"}",
            font_size=36, color=FORMULA_WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, 'A2', 'B5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Geometry setup (conceptual rectangles representing terms)
        blue_rect = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.5, fill_color=BLUE_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_color=BLUE_COLOR)
        red_rect = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1.0, fill_color=RED_COLOR, fill_opacity=0.4, stroke_color=RED_COLOR)
        rects = VGroup(blue_rect, red_rect).arrange(DOWN, buff=0)
        self.place_in_area(rects, 'D2', 'F5')

        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.play(FadeIn(rects))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # L2: "The numerator is the area of our target rectangle."
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        numerator = formula[3]
        arrow_num = Arrow(
            start=numerator.get_bottom() + DOWN * 0.1, 
            end=blue_rect.get_left(), 
            color=BLUE_COLOR, 
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        self.play(
            numerator.animate.set_color(BLUE_COLOR),
            blue_rect.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8),
            Create(arrow_num)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # L3: "The denominator is the sum of all shaded areas."
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        denominator = formula[5]
        # Use a brace to visually group the denominator
        denominator_brace = Brace(denominator, DOWN, color=WHITE, buff=0.1)
        # Arrow from denominator area to the combined rectangles
        arrow_den = Arrow(
            start=denominator_brace.get_bottom(), 
            end=rects.get_bottom() + LEFT * 0.5, 
            color=WHITE, 
            stroke_width=3
        )
        
        self.play(
            FadeOut(arrow_num),
            Create(denominator_brace),
            Create(arrow_den),
            red_rect.animate.set_fill(opacity=0.8)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # L4: "Color-coded labels link the formula to the square's geometry."
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Text labels inside/beside the geometry
        label_num_geom = MathTex(r"P(H) \cdot P(E|H)", font_size=24, color=BLUE_COLOR)
        label_num_geom.move_to(blue_rect.get_center())
        
        label_den_geom = MathTex(r"P(\neg H) \cdot P(E|\neg H)", font_size=24, color=RED_COLOR)
        label_den_geom.move_to(red_rect.get_center())
        
        # Dimensions on the axes of the square/rectangles
        dim_h = MathTex("P(H)", font_size=20, color=BLUE_COLOR).next_to(blue_rect, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        dim_not_h = MathTex("P(\\neg H)", font_size=20, color=RED_COLOR).next_to(red_rect, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        dim_eh = MathTex("P(E|H)", font_size=20, color=BLUE_COLOR).next_to(blue_rect, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(
            FadeOut(denominator_brace),
            FadeOut(arrow_den),
            Write(label_num_geom),
            Write(label_den_geom),
            Write(dim_h),
            Write(dim_not_h),
            Write(dim_eh)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # L5: "Bayes' Theorem turns visual proportions into precise mathematical values."
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(HIGHLIGHT_COLOR)
        
        # Highlight the entire formula for the conclusion
        box = SurroundingRectangle(formula, color=HIGHLIGHT_COLOR, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(Create(box))
        self.wait(3)

from manim import *

class Section6Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Define the Bayes' Theorem formula
        # Part 0: Posterior P(H|E)
        # Part 1: Equals sign
        # Part 2: The fraction P(H)P(E|H) / P(E)
        formula = MathTex(
            r"P(H|E)", 
            r"=", 
            r"\frac{P(H) \cdot P(E|H)}{P(E)}",
            font_size=42
        )
        
        # Center the formula on screen
        formula.move_to(ORIGIN)
        
        # 1. Animation: Write the formula
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # In Manim CE v0.19.0, for a \frac{num}{den} inside a MathTex:
        # Index [0] of the fraction is the horizontal bar
        # Index [1] of the fraction is the numerator
        # Index [2] of the fraction is the denominator
        # Since the fraction is the 3rd argument provided to MathTex, it is formula[2]
        
        try:
            numerator = formula[2][1]
            denominator = formula[2][2]
            
            # 2. Animation: Highlight the components
            self.play(
                numerator.animate.set_color(YELLOW),
                run_time=1.2
            )
            self.play(
                denominator.animate.set_color(BLUE),
                run_time=1.2
            )
            self.wait(1)
            
            # 3. Animation: Focus on the Posterior P(H|E)
            self.play(Indicate(formula[0], color=WHITE))
            self.wait(2)
            
        except IndexError:
            # Fallback if TeX compilation differs: highlight the entire fraction
            self.play(formula[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
            self.wait(2)
